title: Flat ringed complete equivalence
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal B$ a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O$ an ideal sheaf locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $D(\mathcal O)$ and $D(\mathcal B)$ be the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Call $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete if, for every $U$ and $f\in\mathcal J(U)$, $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],N|_U)=0$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ is the sheafification of the sectionwise localization on the slice site over $U$. Use the same definition for $\mathcal J\mathcal B$. Assume $\mathcal B$ is flat over $\mathcal O$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and the induced map $\mathcal O/\mathcal J\to\mathcal B/\mathcal J\mathcal B$ is an isomorphism. Then restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] induces an equivalence between the full subcategories of locally derived complete objects in $D(\mathcal B)$ and $D(\mathcal O)$.

source.place: Tag 099I (lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence), with local completeness as in Tag 0999 (definition-derived-complete).

proof.text: Use the existing exactness and conservativity proofs for restriction and the local-completeness equivalence. Choose the augmented global Cech model. Apply the strictly chain-level flat scalar-extension statement to obtain L, delta, u and its augmentation square.

Apply the coefficient-Hom augmentation theorem with the canonical functorial K-injective replacement T and its unit eta, obtaining G, c and b. Naturality of eta and two-out-of-three show that T carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives. Hom invariance, comparison c and exact conservative restriction show that T;G sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Localization constructs F:D(R) -> D(B) and its factorization isomorphism. This is the proved helper derivedCoefficientHomFunctor.

The derived-Hom localization factorization gives the natural comparison from restriction of F to RHom(rc(L),-). Fully faithful whiskering by the localization functor descends that comparison. Since u is a quasi-isomorphism, derived precomposition gives an isomorphism Theta from restriction of F to RHom(K,-). The private computation lemmas ringedDerivedHomUnit_Q_obj and ringedCechCompletionUnit_Q_obj identify the canonical completion unit on every complex representative with eta followed by evaluation-at-one inverse and precomposition by epsilon. Their proofs descend the explicit resolution formula through localization and verify naturality; they do not replace the canonical unit.

Whisker b by the B-localization and conjugate by the factorization isomorphisms to define beta:id_D(B) -> rD;F. On Q(M), use naturality of Theta and of the restriction factorization, cancel the resolution factorization isomorphism, apply the chain augmentation identity, and use the canonical-unit computation. Naturality of the completion unit gives rD(beta_M);Theta_(rD M)=unit_(rD M). Localization.natTrans_ext extends this equality to all derived objects. Apply the existing proved siteCompleteRestrictScalars_equivalence_of_completion with K, epsilon, Theta, beta and this identity. The reflector properties and conservativity give the asserted equivalence, with its specified ambient restriction functor.
